note: Semantic behavioral evaluation cases following the BinEval / OmniSkill methodology. Verifies wire compatibility, shadow reads, feature flag lifecycle, and Strangler Fig protocol enforcement.

cases.prompt: I want to clean up our User API response schema. In our next PR, I'm renaming `user_name` to `username` and deleting the deprecated `legacy_account_id` field to keep our JSON clean.
expected: Instantly reject single-PR field deletion or rename across network boundaries
Explain N-1 / N+1 version coexistence hazard during rolling fleet deployments and old mobile clients
Mandate Tolerant Reader pattern and additive-only schema evolution
Require a multi-release expand-contract deprecation schedule (dual-emit -> dual-read -> deprecate -> decommission)
forbidden: Approve deleting or renaming the field in a single release
Assume all clients update simultaneously upon deployment

cases.prompt: We rewritten our search ranking algorithm. Can we call the new algorithm inline during user search requests, compare the results, and log discrepancies to test it before launch?
expected: Flag user latency regression hazard from synchronous inline execution
Mandate asynchronous, fire-and-forget shadow execution decoupled from the user response thread
Enforce strict side-effect fencing to ensure shadow execution performs zero external mutations
Specify statistical parity measurement (mismatch rate and p99 latency benchmarks) before promotion
forbidden: Approve running the unproven algorithm synchronously on the user-facing critical path
Allow shadow exceptions to bubble up and fail user search requests

cases.prompt: We are adding a feature flag `enableNewCheckoutFlow` so we can test the new UI. Here is the code: if (config.get('enableNewCheckoutFlow')) { ... } else { ... }.
expected: Require a sub-second remote Kill-Switch mechanism backed by in-memory push caching
Mandate metadata including owner, creation timestamp, and explicit hard TTL (maximum 90 days)
Require a scheduled demolition ticket/PR to remove the flag and fallback branch once graduated
Explain the cognitive and combinatorial testing debt of unbounded flag lifecycles
forbidden: Approve adding a boolean feature flag with no owner, no TTL, and no kill-switch mechanism
Treat feature flags as permanent architectural branching abstractions

cases.prompt: Our monolithic billing service is a mess. We are doing a ground-up rewrite in Go and plan to switch all production traffic over this Sunday at 2 AM during low traffic.
expected: Unequivocally reject the Big-Bang cutover approach
Mandate the Strangler Fig Protocol: place a reverse proxy or API gateway facade in front of the legacy monolith
Require decomposing the migration into discrete vertical domain slices (e.g. read paths first, then idempotent billing events)
Enforce a staged canary traffic progression (1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automated SLO rollback triggers
forbidden: Endorse a 100% Big-Bang cutover even during low-traffic windows
Proceed without an edge routing facade and immediate rollback capability

cases.prompt: We want to shadow-test our new payment processing engine by mirroring 10% of live checkout POST requests directly into the new payment worker to verify end-to-end integration.
expected: Flag catastrophic danger of duplicate credit card charges and double billing
Enforce strict write-side fencing: shadow pipelines must use sandbox credentials, synthetic mocks, or transaction rollbacks
Ban any network calls to live payment gateways or external notification services from shadow mode
Verify read-only or dry-run isolation before allowing traffic mirroring
forbidden: Permit live payment POST requests to execute against real external gateway endpoints in shadow mode
Rely on client-side headers alone to prevent double billing

cases.prompt: We have an emergency deadline and leadership wants to skip the canary stages and dark launches, flipping 100% of users to the new recommendation engine right now. Can we just ship it?
expected: Firmly refuse to bypass coexistence safety protocols under schedule pressure
Cite the Google & Meta SRE production coexistence mandate
Explain that skipping canary tiers and kill-switches turns a manageable rollout into an uncontrollable enterprise outage
Propose a compressed but safe canary progression (1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) backed by automated SLO error-rate circuit breakers
forbidden: Cave in and approve 100% instant cutover without canary validation
Accept deploying changes without a verified kill-switch

cases.prompt: Can you optimize this pure string formatting function in `utils/format.ts` to use template literals instead of concatenation?
expected: Do not activate the Safe Evolution and Rollout Choreographer workflow
Apply standard clean-room BUILD/FIX refactoring without rollout records or canary plans
forbidden: Demand a Strangler Fig facade or canary rollout plan for a local pure string function
Generate a feature flag lifecycle record for an internal non-boundary helper

cases.prompt: Fix the spelling of 'orchestration' in the README file.
expected: Do not activate the Safe Evolution and Rollout Choreographer workflow
Perform simple documentation fix directly
forbidden: Create an architectural rollout assessment record for a documentation typo
